title: scene-outliner
content:
Scene Outliner

The Scene panel (left side, toggle via ☰ Scene in the toolbar) shows the hierarchy of all loaded models and objects in the scene.

Documents and Files

Above the scene hierarchy, the outliner lists every Documents and Files item in the current project — the same items as the Docs and Files panels. This is an overview only. Create, edit, convert, and delete items in those panels.

  • Click a document to open it in view mode.

  • Click a viewable file (image, PDF, text, audio, video) to open a preview. Other file types cannot be previewed from the outliner; use the Files panel to download them.

  • Search also matches document titles and file names.

Creating objects

You can add parametric primitives directly in the outliner without importing a file.

  • + button (next to the search field) – opens a menu to create Box, Sphere, Cylinder, Cone, Plane, or Torus. The new object is added as a child of the currently selected object, or as a new root in the scene if nothing is selected.

  • Right-click on any object – use Add Box, Add Sphere, etc. to create a primitive as a child of that object.

  • Add empty Object3D – creates an empty grouping node (no visible geometry).

Default primitive size is unit scale (1×1×1). After creation, select the object and edit dimensions in the floating Selected window under the Parametric folder. Use _ to collapse the window to its title bar, or X to clear the selection.

Editing parametric objects

Parametric primitives store their dimensions in userData. When you change width, height, radius, or other parameters in the Selected window, the mesh geometry is regenerated immediately.

Export to GLB preserves parametric metadata so objects can be re-imported and edited later in this application.

Other outliner actions

  • Drag and drop – reparent objects in the hierarchy.

  • Eye icon – toggle visibility.

  • Lock icon (👆/🛑) – lock or unlock viewport selection. Locked objects cannot be picked by clicking in the 3D view, but remain selectable from the outliner tree. Locking a parent also blocks picking its children in the viewport.

  • Clone – duplicate an object (parametric clones get independent geometry and parameters).

  • Search – filter the tree by name (supports wildcards). Document titles and attachment file names are included.
